# Tinlance Agent Platform

> Governed execution substrate for secure autonomous AI agents, beneath Tinlance Agentic OS.

## Canonical documentation

- [README](README.md): product scope, quick start, installation, usage, configuration, features, and boundaries.
- [Architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md): stable system boundary and security invariants.
- [Documentation index](docs/README.md): documentation organized by purpose.
- [Roadmap](docs/ROADMAP.md): canonical M0-M14 sequence and post-M14 enterprise assurance history.
- [Enterprise baseline](docs/ENTERPRISE-BASELINE.md): production acceptance and external-dependency evidence requirements.
- [Enterprise conformance](docs/ENTERPRISE-CONFORMANCE.md): conformance contracts and evidence expectations.

- [Release security](docs/RELEASE-SECURITY.md): signed-release and SBOM verification guidance.

- [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md): contribution workflow and engineering constraints.
- [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md): release and engineering history.

## Product boundary

Tinlance Agent Platform owns identity, tenancy, authorization, policy, approval, runtime, model/tool/MCP mediation, sandbox, secrets, budgets, evidence, audit, and governed execution.

Tinlance Agentic OS and domain systems consume stable contracts and SDK surfaces. The Platform does not absorb application or domain responsibilities.

## Security model

Core properties are deny-by-default authorization, immutable tenant scope, complete mediation, exact and expiring approval binding, non-escalating child-agent authority, fail-closed isolation, execution-only secret handling, attributable integrity-protected evidence, and sensitive-data-safe observability.

## Important limitation

Repository CI demonstrates repository controls and executable tests. It does not by itself prove that external production infrastructure, independent penetration testing, disaster recovery exercises, or customer compliance evidence exists.

## Machine-readable source

The repository is Python-based, requires Python 3.12 through 3.14, and is built with Hatchling. Tests are configured through pyproject.toml.
